transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-11 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Evan, Priya, Marta, Samir, Lena, Theo + several observers (org-wide invite)
Shared artifacts: playbook draft (https://redwood.internal/playbooks/runtime-fallback-v2), canary config gist (https://gist.github.com/rwd/canary-20260611), slides: https://redwood.app/launch-playbook-deck

[00:00] Evan Brooks: Okay everyone, uh, thanks for carving out time. Purpose — run through the fallback playbook, simulate a few abort scenarios and make sure owners are clear. I'll kick off with a quick framing.
[00:18] Evan Brooks: We're focusing on three realistic failure modes: kernel OOM that causes per-node meltdown, runaway token generation pushing cost and latency, and KV cache invalidation storms after a model swap.
[00:35] Priya Nair: Quick note — when we say "runaway token" we mean either model hallucination loops or an input that bypasses stop tokens, but observability hasn't caught the early curvature. We need earlier hooks.
[00:50] Marta Ruiz: Right, and the runtime's current backoff is node-level; it doesn't surface as a customer-facing degrade — it just slows all sharded requests which then cascades. That's why fallback routing is critical.
[01:10] Lena Gomez: On monitoring, we have token-rate panels, but the alert threshold is high. We should add a derivative alert and an alert for cost-per-minute per-route.
[01:28] Theo Park: Also I want to surface that our current canary tooling only does header-based shifts. For a fallback we need control-plane tools that shift by percentage and have an automatic revert on latency SLA breach.
[01:45] Evan Brooks: Great. Let's run a tabletop. Scenario 1: after a staged release of a quantized model variant, we see a spike in 95th-percentile latency in region-us-east-1 and per-token cost doubles on a specific route. Who detects first?
[02:05] Priya Nair: Oncall will get latency alerts — 95th goes over SLO. But this is ambiguous: is it pure latency or a throughput saturation?
[02:18] Marta Ruiz: Runtime metrics show KV hit rate drops to 10% — so it's cache miss storming, likely due to incorrect prefix mapping after the model swap. That explains per-token work increase.
[02:34] Lena Gomez: Observability: we will see increased backend token count and degraded cache hit metric. We need a composite alert that ties 95p latency + cache_miss_rate > 0.4.
[02:48] Evan Brooks: Action: Priya to own the composite alert spec. If composite fires, we follow playbook step 2 — run quick-kill to divert traffic to previous model variant.
[03:02] Marta Ruiz: The 'quick-kill' endpoint — current sketch in playbook: POST /admin/v1/fallback with body {route, model_variant, ttl_seconds}. It needs auth, audit logging, and metrics emission.
[03:18] Theo Park: Implementation detail — this endpoint must only be callable by release-engineer or SRE group, and should generate a trace id for rollback. We also need to ensure control-plane caches are invalidated in a safe order.
[03:35] Samir Patel: Customer comms: when we divert, do we proactively tell customers? For Hosted customers we can update the status page; for Dedicated we need to ensure local contract limits. Also legal wants the KB language to avoid implying data loss.
[03:52] Evan Brooks: Yes. Samir will draft KB wording. We'll include explicit language: "fallback to prior verified model variant; latency/behavior may differ; no data is deleted."
[04:07] Scenario 2: A kernel OOM occurs in a GPU pool causing many requests to queue and error. We need rapid mitigations and graceful degradation.
[04:22] Marta Ruiz: For kernel OOM, runtime suggests retiring nodes from the rotation, draining inflight requests and shifting to spare capacity. But we need a policy for how much spare to keep — current autoscaler often waits too long.
[04:36] Priya Nair: We should have a hard lower bound on spare GPUs for critical tiers. For Dedicated customers, we can fall back to cheaper model variants in the same pool to preserve throughput.
[04:50] Theo Park: Also fallback route should prefer model-compat variants that are quantized. We may need a model-compat mapping table in the control plane.
[05:06] Evan Brooks: Good. Let's simulate an abort: runtime declares 60% of pool degraded. Who pulls the trigger on full rollback?
[05:18] Priya Nair: Oncall can escalate to SRE lead after 5 minutes of sustained SLO breach. SRE lead + Release Eng must sign off on full rollback. We should have pre-registered approvers to avoid pager-chase.
[05:34] Marta Ruiz: We also need a neat metric threshold: 5-minute 95p > 2x baseline AND error-rate > 1% triggers canary abort.
[05:46] Evan Brooks: Note for playbook: add explicit decision tree with metrics, minimum approvers, and a time window. Evan adds that item.
[05:55] [crosstalk] Unidentified: (murmurs) — add that to the runbook.
[06:05] Scenario 3: KV cache invalidation after model swap causes session-level prefix mismatch and user sessions get inconsistent completions.
[06:20] Marta Ruiz: This is tricky because prefix caching is per-model checksum. If we swap a model, the prefix mappings misalign and we get long tail misses. The mitigation path: stagger key-rotation, flush hot key ranges slowly, or fall back to previous model for affected sessions.
[06:40] Lena Gomez: Observability must be able to tie session IDs to cache-hit metrics. Right now session_id exists in logs but not surfaced in dashboards.
[06:54] Theo Park: That requires a short-term ingest pipeline update — add session_id to the KV hit telemetry and sample. We can do that in a day but need to be careful about cardinality.
[07:10] Evan Brooks: Let's call this: Theo to scope a low-cardinality sampling approach; Marta to add a safety step in deployment: "do not change model checksum and cache mapping until 10m after traffic shift".
[07:25] Samir Patel: From product/CS side, if cache miss causes user-visible regressions, customer success should be looped immediately; predefined messages will help.
[07:38] Evan Brooks: Okay, moving to the playbook sections that need fill-in. I've highlighted five gaps in the doc: 1) Quick-kill auth/audit detail; 2) Composite alert spec; 3) Canary abort thresholds; 4) Ownership matrix for each step; 5) Customer KB draft. We'll assign owners now.
[07:55] Priya Nair: I'll take composite alert spec and oncall escalation policy.
[08:00] Lena Gomez: I'll own the dashboard updates and token-cost alert panels.
[08:05] Marta Ruiz: I'll implement quick-kill and the model-compat mapping table.
[08:10] Theo Park: I'll wire up the canary traffic-shift script and make it revertable.
[08:14] Samir Patel: I'll do the KB and external comms draft.
[08:18] Evan Brooks: I'll update the rollout checklist and add the decision tree.
[08:22] [15:00] — mid-meeting stretch/side chat — watchers join
[15:30] Priya Nair: A quick technical debt note: our autoscaler estimator doesn't take into account KV cache heat; it forecasts by GPU utilization only. If we add KV miss factor we'll be better prepared.
[15:46] Marta Ruiz: Also, when we talk about quantized fallback models, note that outputs may change in wording and temperature — we need sanity tests in the canary to validate semantic parity, not just latency.
[16:05] Lena Gomez: On sanity tests: we should have a small eval corpus with business-critical prompts and guardrail thresholds. If the model fails more than X% of the corpus, automatic abort.
[16:22] Evan Brooks: Let's define X as 10% for now for canaries; we can tune after first run. Theo — include a simple eval harness that runs 50 prompts during the canary.
[16:36] Theo Park: Yep, will do. Also want to call out the need for a rollback rehearsal in the staging cluster — runbook step to rehearse within 48 hours of any new major rollout.
[16:50] Samir Patel: Legal asks: ensure KB avoids commitments that conflict with our SLAs for Dedicated customers. We'll run the KB text by legal before publishing.
[17:03] Priya Nair: For ownership handoff, we should have a short template that states who is the decision maker by time-window (0-5min: oncall, 5-30min: SRE lead, >30min: Eng Director). That prevents finger-pointing.
[17:18] Evan Brooks: We'll add that to the playbook.
[17:23] [25:00] — quick simulation exercise (live) — Theo flips 10% traffic to new variant while Lena watches dashboards
[25:12] Theo Park: Flipped 10% now — watch the 95p and the eval corpus — running the 50 prompts.
[25:28] Lena Gomez: Seeing slight bump, 95p + 12% on token per request. Eval harness showing 6% failure vs baseline.
[25:45] Marta Ruiz: Cache hit rate dropped from 78% to 48% on that route — that's big.
[26:03] Evan Brooks: This triggers the canary abort rule (eval failures >10%? It's 6% now, but cache drop is severe). Should we abort?
[26:18] Priya Nair: Not yet — metric threshold not met, but we should elevate. If composite alert fires in next 2 minutes, do quick-kill.
[26:30] Theo Park: I'm going to push a simulated cache flush to reproduce worst-case.
[26:46] [noise] Theo Park: flushed hot keys — watch the hit rate.
[26:55] Lena Gomez: Now hit rate down to 35%, eval failures 14%. That crosses our temporary cutoff.
[27:06] Evan Brooks: Ok that's a hard trigger — Priya, perform quick-kill.
[27:12] Priya Nair: Executing POST /admin/v1/fallback ... (typing) — note: on the real run we must ensure rotation TTL 600s.
[27:24] Marta Ruiz: Received the fallback command — traffic shifting in progress. Rolling back 10% to 0%
[27:38] Lena Gomez: 95p back to baseline, eval harness shows 2% failure. All good.
[27:52] Evan Brooks: That was a successful run. Lessons: need lower thresholds perhaps, and quicker composite alert wiring.
[28:08] [30:00] — planning next items: runbook hygiene and drills
[30:20] Evan Brooks: We'll schedule the tabletop with the oncall team next Tuesday. Priya will own calendar invites. Theo, can you automate a canary job that we can trigger from #releases channel?
[30:34] Theo Park: Yes, will wire a slash-command that triggers the canary and records the trace id.
[30:40] Samir Patel: Also we should prepare a one-page customer-facing summary describing what fallback means for Dedicated customers — impact on SLAs, expected behavioral differences, and contact points.
[30:56] Evan Brooks: Add that as a deliverable.
[31:05] [closing] Evan Brooks: Quick recap: owners assigned, action items captured, simulation succeeded. Next steps — Priya to coordinate tabletop, Theo + Marta to implement quick-kill and canary automation, Lena to tighten alerts, Samir to author KB, Evan to update the decision tree and roll checklist. I'll post the updated playbook by EOD Monday and share the canary logs.
[31:35] Priya Nair: One more ask — add runbook step for legal & CS notification for Dedicated customers upon fallback.
[31:45] Samir Patel: Noted — will include that in the KB draft.
[31:50] Evan Brooks: Thanks everyone. Meeting adjourned.
